From 7dd47617114921fdd8c095509e5e7b4373cc44a1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Date: Tue, 26 Mar 2019 22:51:02 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] watchdog: Respect watchdog cpumask on CPU hotplug

The rework of the watchdog core to use cpu_stop_work broke the watchdog
cpumask on CPU hotplug.

The watchdog_enable/disable() functions are now called unconditionally from
the hotplug callback, i.e. even on CPUs which are not in the watchdog
cpumask. As a consequence the watchdog can become unstoppable.

Only invoke them when the plugged CPU is in the watchdog cpumask.

Fixes: 9cf57731b63e ("watchdog/softlockup: Replace "watchdog/%u" threads with cpu_stop_work")
Reported-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Tested-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: Oleg Nesterov <oleg@redhat.com>
Cc: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Cc: Nicholas Piggin <npiggin@gmail.com>
Cc: Don Zickus <dzickus@redhat.com>
Cc: Ricardo Neri <ricardo.neri-calderon@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/alpine.DEB.2.21.1903262245490.1789@nanos.tec.linutronix.de

diff --git a/kernel/watchdog.c b/kernel/watchdog.c
index 403c9bd90413..6a5787233113 100644
--- a/kernel/watchdog.c
+++ b/kernel/watchdog.c
@@ -554,13 +554,15 @@ static void softlockup_start_all(void)
 
 int lockup_detector_online_cpu(unsigned int cpu)
 {
-	watchdog_enable(cpu);
+	if (cpumask_test_cpu(cpu, &watchdog_allowed_mask))
+		watchdog_enable(cpu);
 	return 0;
 }
 
 int lockup_detector_offline_cpu(unsigned int cpu)
 {
-	watchdog_disable(cpu);
+	if (cpumask_test_cpu(cpu, &watchdog_allowed_mask))
+		watchdog_disable(cpu);
 	return 0;
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/watchdog.c`**
- The `lockup_detector_online_cpu` function was modified to conditionally call `watchdog_enable(cpu)` only if the CPU being plugged in is part of the `watchdog_allowed_mask`.
- Similarly, the `lockup_detector_offline_cpu` function was modified to conditionally call `watchdog_disable(cpu)` only if the CPU being unplugged is part of the `watchdog_allowed_mask`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `kernel/watchdog.c` are directly related to the issue of the watchdog cpumask not being respected during CPU hotplug operations. By adding checks to ensure that the `watchdog_enable` and `watchdog_disable` functions are only invoked for CPUs that are included in the `watchdog_allowed_mask`, the patch addresses the bug where the watchdog could become unstoppable when these functions were called unconditionally. This change ensures that the watchdog functionality is correctly managed in accordance with the CPU's membership in the cpumask, thereby preventing unintended behavior during CPU hotplug events.

Here is the commit message:
watchdog: Respect watchdog cpumask on CPU hotplug

The rework of the watchdog core to use cpu_stop_work broke the watchdog
cpumask on CPU hotplug.

The watchdog_enable/disable() functions are now called unconditionally from
the hotplug callback, i.e. even on CPUs which are not in the watchdog
cpumask. As a consequence the watchdog can become unstoppable.

Only invoke them when the plugged CPU is in the watchdog cpumask.

Fixes: 9cf57731b63e ("watchdog/softlockup: Replace "watchdog/%u" threads with cpu_stop_work")
Reported-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Tested-by: Maxime Coquelin <maxime.coquelin@redhat.com>
Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>

Cc: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Cc: Nicholas Piggin <npiggin@gmail.com>
Cc: Don Zickus <dzickus@redhat.com>
Cc: Ricardo Neri <ricardo.neri-calderon@linux.intel.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/alpine.DEB.2.21.1903262245490.1789@nanos.tec.linutronix.de

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the unconditional invocation of `watchdog_enable` and `watchdog_disable` functions during CPU hotplug operations, regardless of whether the CPU was part of the `watchdog_allowed_mask`. This led to situations where the watchdog could become unstoppable on CPUs that were not intended to be monitored by the watchdog.

Here is the patch:
 
 int lockup_detector_online_cpu(unsigned int cpu)
 {
-	watchdog_enable(cpu);
+	if (cpumask_test_cpu(cpu, &watchdog_allowed_mask))
+		watchdog_enable(cpu);
 	return 0;
 }
 
 int lockup_detector_offline_cpu(unsigned int cpu)
 {
-	watchdog_disable(cpu);
+	if (cpumask_test_cpu(cpu, &watchdog_allowed_mask))
+		watchdog_disable(cpu);
 	return 0;
 }
